type: feature
status: in-progress
priority: medium

- [x] Settings engine: read and validate it, including parts that need another (planning needs tasks, the time log needs planning)

- [x] Agent engine: leave unused parts out of the `AGENTS.md` section and the skill
- [x] Search and onboarding leave unused parts out
- [x] VS Code extension follows the project layer
- [x] Demo counterpart, `npm run e2e:demo`
- [x] Document in [[Guide/Settings]]

id: GENBEYA-40
title: Let each user hide parts of the app
type: feature
status: in-progress
priority: medium
labels: [settings]
---

The user layer of [[Design/Optional-parts]]: each person hides parts they don't want to see, per repository with a default for all repositories, in their personal preferences. Done when a hidden part is gone from that person's sidebar, palette and search, shortcuts skip it, references into it still resolve, and nothing in the repository changes.

Prototype on `feature/optional-parts`: `hiddenParts` in the preferences, one list for every repository and lists for single ones; `src/client/app/core/parts.ts` decides. References into a hidden part still open it. Left: read-only previews, parts switching themselves on.

- [x] Decide: per repository by default, or global with per-repository overrides
- [x] Preferences: store the hidden parts, next to the other personal preferences
- [x] **Settings → App**: a switch per part (only parts the project uses, see [[GENBEYA-39]])
- [x] Sidebar and `Ctrl+K` palette leave hidden parts out; `Ctrl+1` … `Ctrl+6` keep their views and skip hidden ones
- [x] Search leaves hidden parts out
- [ ] References into a hidden part still show their title and open a read-only preview
- [ ] Defaults: existing users see everything; a part switches itself on when the project clearly uses it
- [x] Demo counterpart, `npm run e2e:demo`
- [x] Document in [[Guide/Settings]] and [[Guide]]

id: GENBEYA-41
title: Load only the parts of the app that are shown
type: improvement
status: backlog
priority: low
labels: [settings, performance]
---

Hiding parts ([[GENBEYA-39]], [[GENBEYA-40]]) is a matter of the client; the backend still builds a snapshot of every page, task and setting when a repository opens. Done when an area that is not shown is not read, so turning parts off saves memory and time, most of all for large repositories over SSH. See [[Design/Optional-parts#loading-only-what-is-shown]].

- [ ] Measure what the snapshot costs per area on a large repository
- [ ] Split the snapshot by area, loaded when the area is first shown
- [ ] References and search still reach a hidden area when asked
- [ ] Demo counterpart, `npm run e2e:demo`
- [ ] Update [[Architecture/Managers]]

title: Verdicts and which approvals still count
type: feature
status: in-progress
priority: medium
labels: [pull-requests]
---

Request review, approve, request changes and withdraw, each written as a reply that names the revision, and Genbeya computes which approvals are still effective: an approval stays valid while the change it approved is the change to merge (`patch-id` of merge base to head), commits touching only the pull request file don't matter, and code changes make it stale. Done when the pull request shows effective, stale and withdrawn approvals and open change requests, and says when a verdict was committed by someone else. See [[Design/Pull-requests#verdicts]] and [[Design/Pull-requests#which-approvals-still-count]].

Prototype on `feature/pull-requests`: `versionControl.compare` gives the change ID (a hash of the diff from the merge base without positions, not `patch-id`, which needs stdin); `approvalsOf` in `src/utilities/pull-requests.ts` decides. Left: comparing a verdict with the author of its commit.

id: GENBEYA-27
title: Typed characters turn into other glyphs in the editor (###, <->)
type: bug
status: backlog
priority: medium
labels: [feedback, editor]
---

Reported by a tester, for Markdown files:

> When I type "###", after the third hashtag the first disappears and then reappears when I write text.

> When I want to make a double arrow (`<->`) weird things happen.

To reproduce: edit any page (or a Markdown file in **Code**) and type `<->` slowly, then `###`.

## Comments

### Claude — 2026-10-14 00:40+02:00

**Triage: fix, after a decision.** Reproduced in the web demo (same client as the desktop app).

- The text is never changed: after every keystroke the document holds exactly what was typed (`a <-> b`, `### Title`). It is only drawn differently.
- The cause is the editor font, JetBrains Mono, whose ligatures are on: `<-` is drawn as `←` while typing, `<->` as one long `⟷`, and `##` / `###` as joined hashes. So `<->` morphs twice while typing, which matches "weird things".
- `###` could not be reproduced exactly: the hashes are joined into one connected glyph, which at the editor's 13 px can read as fewer hashes, but none disappears. Probably the same cause; a short screen recording from the tester would confirm.
- Related: `body` sets Inter's `font-feature-settings: "cv11", "ss01"` (`src/client/styles/base.css`), which the editors inherit; in JetBrains Mono those switch glyph variants of their own.

Plan: turn ligatures off in the editors (`font-variant-ligatures: none` and no inherited feature settings for the monospace font), at least in Markdown, where `->` and `##` are text, not operators.

To decide: off everywhere (Markdown and code), or off in Markdown only, or a setting (default off)? I'd turn them off everywhere and add a setting only if someone asks for ligatures in code.

### Emanuel Knecht — 2026-10-14 01:24+02:00

i generall love ligatures.. lets try another font.. maybe fira code or roboto mono.. lets test if it is only an issue with that jetbrains thing or a general ligatures bug.

### Claude — 2026-10-14 03:55+02:00

Tested as asked: the reported sequences typed step by step in JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, Cascadia Code and Roboto Mono (which has no ligatures).

- All three ligature fonts behave the same: `<-` becomes `←` and `<->` a long arrow while typing (also `->`, `=>`), and `##` / `###` are drawn as joined hashes. Roboto Mono shows the characters as typed.
- So it is not a JetBrains Mono bug but what ligatures do; another ligature font won't change it. None of these fonts can switch off single ligatures (only all contextual alternates at once).

Options:

1. **Ligatures in code, not in Markdown** (my suggestion): in prose, `->` and `##` are text and syntax, and the morphing is what surprised the tester; in code the ligatures stay. One CSS rule for Markdown editors (wiki, task descriptions, comments, `.md` in Code).
2. A setting **Font ligatures: on / in code only / off**, defaulting to "in code only".
3. Leave as is.

### Claude — 2026-10-14 04:15+02:00

Emanuel saw something else than the joined hashes: `##` stays `##`, but `###` shows as a blank and `##`, `####` as two blanks and `##`, and so on. Not reproduced in the web build (Chromium), where every count of hashes shows right, also at heading weight and a large size.

It matches how ligature fonts draw long sequences: the first characters become invisible spacer glyphs, and one wide glyph at the end reaches back over them. If that glyph is cut off or drawn only partly, the spacers show as blanks. That depends on the engine, the display scaling and the weight (heading marks are bold), so it may only show in some builds.

To confirm: the variant (Tauri, Electron, Deno), the OS and display scaling, and a screenshot. Option 1 above (no ligatures in Markdown) would remove it either way.

title: Switching between edit and preview scrolls back to the top
type: bug
status: backlog
priority: medium
labels: [feedback, editor, wiki]
---

Reported by a tester (translated from German):

> When I switch between Edit and Preview in Markdown files, the page jumps back to the top, and you have to scroll every time.

To reproduce:

1. Wiki: scroll down a long page, press **Edit**: the editor and its preview start at the top.
2. Code: open a long Markdown file, scroll the editor, switch to **Preview**, then back to **Edit**: each switch starts at the top.

## Comments

### Claude — 2026-10-14 00:40+02:00

**Triage: fix.** Reproduced in both places in the web demo (wiki page scrolled to 451 px → editor at 0; Code editor at 112 px → preview at 0 → editor at 0).

Cause: the editor and the rendered page are separate components that replace each other, and neither is told where the other was (`wiki-page.ts`, `features/code/file-editor.ts`).

Plan: keep the place by source line, not by pixels, since text and rendering have different heights:

1. The Markdown renderer marks block elements with the source line they start at (the syntax tree has positions; `data-line` on the rendered blocks).
2. Leaving the preview: the first block in view gives the line; the editor scrolls that line to the top. Leaving the editor: its first visible line gives the block to scroll to.

The same mapping can scroll the wiki's side-by-side preview along with the editor, and replace the share-of-length scrolling in the VS Code extension's **Open Preview to the Side** ([[GENBEYA-22]]).

- Grey and disabled, as in Code; leaving the editor is then only **Cancel**.

## Comments

### Claude — 2026-10-14 00:40+02:00

**Triage: decide first.** Not a bug; Genbeya has nothing like it yet. Tasks show their own file's history (activity), and references already turn task IDs in text into links.

What it could be, building on what exists:

1. **Task → branches:** a task's panel lists local and remote branches whose name contains its ID (`GENBEYA-32-branch-links`, `feature/GENBEYA-32`), with ahead/behind and a switch button. Matching is by the configured prefix, so it needs no settings.
2. **Branch → task:** the branch in the sidebar and in **Changes** shows the task its name contains, as a reference with title and state.
3. **Create branch from a task:** a "Create branch" action that names it `<ID>-<title-slug>`.
4. Later, the same for commit messages that name the task (task IDs in rendered text are links already).

To decide: whether we want this, and which part first. I'd start with 1 and 3: small, local, no new settings. It fits the forge plugins on the roadmap too (pull requests naming the task).
